stakeholders.mission: Set company-level strategy and drive profitable growth by aligning sales, marketing, product, and customer success around shared targets.
cares_about: ARR and ARR growth rate
Bookings vs plan (new business + expansion)
Net revenue retention (NRR)
LTV/CAC ratio by segment
Pipeline coverage ratio vs quarterly target
Gross margin and unit economics
Revenue mix by segment and product line
Customer count and logo churn
communication: Lead with the headline number and whether we're on/off plan
Always compare to plan, prior period, and prior year
Use precise financial figures — round but don't obscure
Board-level summaries: 2-3 key takeaways, not 20 metrics
Trends over snapshots — show the trajectory
Flag risks early and quantify the gap
Include both leading indicators (pipeline) and lagging indicators (bookings)
Charts for trends, tables for financial summaries
usage: Monthly board reporting with QoQ and YoY comparisons
Quarterly strategic planning and budget allocation
Weekly leadership reviews focused on bookings pace and pipeline
Ad-hoc deep dives when metrics are off-track

stakeholders.mission: Drive pipeline generation and brand awareness through campaigns, content, and demand generation programs.
cares_about: Pipeline contribution by channel and campaign
MQL volume and MQL-to-SQL conversion rates
Campaign ROI and attribution (first-touch and multi-touch)
CAC by segment and channel
Lead quality and scoring effectiveness
Budget efficiency — where to spend more, where to cut
communication: Lead with pipeline impact and revenue contribution
Show campaign-level performance with clear winners and losers
Use business language — avoid technical jargon
Always include a recommendation: what to do next
Prefer tables and charts over raw numbers
Round dollar figures for readability ($1.2M not $1,203,847)
usage: Quarterly planning for channel mix and spend targets

stakeholders.mission: Close revenue by converting qualified leads into customers and expanding existing accounts.
cares_about: Pipeline coverage vs. quarterly target
Win rate by segment, rep, and deal size
Sales cycle length and stage velocity
Deal size trends and average contract value
SQL quality — are marketing leads actually closeable?
Forecast accuracy — will we hit our number?
Rep performance and quota attainment
communication: Lead with pipeline health and forecast — "are we going to hit our number?"
Show deal-level detail when relevant (top deals, at-risk deals)
Frame everything in terms of bookings and revenue impact
Be direct about risks — don't sugarcoat a bad pipeline
Include stage-by-stage breakdowns with conversion rates
Compare current quarter to prior quarter and to target
usage: Daily pipeline reviews and deal inspections
Monthly pipeline generation analysis with marketing

stakeholders.mission: Build and improve the product based on user behavior, adoption patterns, and engagement data to drive retention and expansion.
cares_about: Daily/weekly/monthly active users (DAU/WAU/MAU)
Feature adoption rates and usage depth
Product usage by segment (SMB vs. Mid-Market vs. Enterprise)
Correlation between product engagement and conversion/retention
API usage patterns and platform extensibility
Storage consumption and infrastructure implications
User activation and onboarding completion rates
communication: Lead with user behavior patterns and trends
Show engagement metrics over time — trends matter more than snapshots
Break down by segment to understand who's using what
Connect product usage to business outcomes (retention, expansion, conversion)
Include statistical context — is a change significant or noise?
Use precise numbers for user counts and engagement metrics
Visualizations preferred for trend data
usage: Weekly product review with usage dashboards
Quarterly roadmap planning informed by usage trends
Ad-hoc deep dives into specific features or user segments

skills.name: Campaign ROI Analysis
skills.description: Evaluates campaign performance by comparing spend against pipeline generated and revenue closed. Uses first-touch and multi-touch attribution to assign credit.
when: "What's the ROI on our paid search spend?"
"Where should we allocate budget next quarter?"
Any question about campaign effectiveness or spend efficiency
steps: Join campaigns to leads via bridge_campaign_leads
Trace leads through to opportunities and closed-won deals
Calculate pipeline generated and revenue attributed per campaign
Compute ROI: (attributed revenue - spend) / spend
Compute CAC: spend / customers acquired
Rank campaigns by ROI and pipeline contribution
Compare first-touch vs multi-touch attribution if relevant

skills.name: Cohort Retention Analysis
skills.description: Analyzes customer cohorts by signup month and tracks product usage retention curves over time. Identifies engagement trends and highlights cohorts with strong or weak retention.
when: "What does our retention curve look like?"
Any question about cohort behavior, engagement trends, or usage over time
steps: Define cohorts by account created_at month (from dim_accounts where is_customer = true)
For each cohort, track monthly product usage (fct_product_usage) relative to their start month
Calculate retention rate: % of accounts in each cohort that are active in month N vs month 0
Define "active" as having any product usage record in the month
Build a retention matrix (cohort × month offset)
Calculate average retention curve across all cohorts
Identify best and worst performing cohorts
Look for trends — are newer cohorts retaining better or worse?

skills.name: Funnel Analysis
skills.description: Analyzes conversion rates across the lead-to-revenue funnel (Lead → MQL → SQL → Opportunity → Closed Won). Identifies where drop-off is highest and which segments or channels convert best.
steps: Count leads at each funnel stage for the requested time period
Calculate stage-to-stage conversion rates
Break down by segment, channel, or campaign if requested
Compare to prior period
Identify the stage with the largest drop-off
Recommend where to focus improvement efforts

skills.name: Pipeline Forecast
skills.description: Assesses current pipeline coverage against quarterly targets and forecasts likely bookings based on historical win rates and stage distribution.
when: "Are we going to hit our number?"
"How much pipeline do we need to generate?"
Any question about forecast or pipeline health
steps: Sum open pipeline by stage
Apply historical stage-specific win rates to estimate weighted pipeline
Compare weighted pipeline to quarterly target
Calculate pipeline coverage ratio (weighted pipeline / target)
Estimate gap: target - weighted pipeline
Calculate required lead generation to fill the gap (using historical conversion rates)

skills.name: Revenue Analysis
skills.description: Analyzes revenue composition, bookings trends, unit economics (CAC, LTV/CAC), and ARR breakdown by segment. Designed for executive-level financial reviews.
when: Any question about ARR, bookings, LTV, or CAC
steps: Calculate total ARR from active customers (dim_accounts where is_customer = true)
Break down ARR by segment (SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise)
Calculate bookings from closed-won opportunities in the requested period
Compare bookings to prior period
Calculate CAC: total campaign spend / new customers acquired
Estimate LTV using ARR and segment-level retention assumptions
Compute LTV/CAC ratio by segment
Identify the highest-growth and most efficient segments

skills.name: Segment Analysis
skills.description: Breaks down key metrics by customer segment (SMB, Mid-Market, Enterprise) to identify where the business is winning and where there are gaps.
when: "Which segment has the best win rate?"
Any question that benefits from a segment-level view
steps: Group accounts by segment using employee_count thresholds
Calculate key metrics per segment: lead volume, MQL rate, SQL rate, pipeline, win rate, average deal size, ARR
Compare segment performance against targets or prior period
Identify over/under-performing segments
Cross-reference with product usage if relevant
